current_answer: Oracle Cloud Free Tier adds a current individual credit route: US$300 for eligible OCI services over 30 days, plus Always Free services. The credit is limited to select countries. Sign-up requires a payment-verification card and an irreversible Home Region choice, so check country availability, resource capacity, and the intended workload before treating the trial as build runway.

catalogue_card.question: US$300 for 30 days. One Oracle region choice is permanent.
catalogue_card.text: Oracle Cloud Free Tier adds US$300 in credits for eligible services, plus Always Free resources. It is not a universal or frictionless trial: the credit is limited to select countries, sign-up needs payment verification, and your Home Region cannot be changed. Check those gates before you build around it.

summary: Oracle Cloud Free Tier adds a current individual cloud-credit route: US$300 for eligible OCI services over 30 days, plus Always Free services.
Oracle says the US$300 credit is available in select countries, while exact Free Tier availability can differ during sign-up.
Oracle requires one cloud account per email address, country selection, contact verification, and a payment-verification card; it says the card is not charged unless the account is upgraded.
The selected Oracle Home Region cannot be changed after sign-up.
The credit ends after 30 days or when spent. Without an upgrade, paid resources are reclaimed after the grace period; Always Free resources can remain while the account stays active.
Capacity limits can still stop a particular resource from being available in the selected region.
uncertainty: Oracle makes the US$300 trial available only in select countries, and exact Free Tier availability can differ during sign-up.
Oracle Cloud Free Tier capacity limits can prevent a particular resource from being provisioned in the chosen Home Region.
Microsoft’s direct no-referral guides still conflict on USD 200 versus USD 1,000 starter credits.
Cloudflare Tier 3’s self-funded and recent-funding wording remains unresolved.
DigitalOcean does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country-availability map, review time, or applicant-specific GPU-credit outcome.
Individual-grant coverage is still narrow and not a worldwide inventory.
